title: Check-then-act and read-modify-write
points: Check-then-act: a thread checks a condition and then acts on it, but another thread can change the condition between the check and the act.
Read-modify-write: a thread reads a value, computes a new one and writes it back, so two threads can read the same old value and one update is lost.
Both are race conditions because the check/read and the act/write are separate steps that can interleave across threads.
The fix is to make the whole sequence atomic: put it under a lock or, for a single variable, use an atomic variable.
trade: Check-then-act typically involves a condition over state (is the seat free?), so it needs a lock around check and act together. Read-modify-write on a single counter can use an atomic variable instead (e.g. incrementAndGet). Note: a volatile field gives visibility but does NOT make count++ atomic.
test: Two users book the last seat at the same instant and both get a confirmation. Which race pattern is this and what makes it go away?
answer: Check-then-act: both saw the seat free before either booked it. Make check and book one atomic step, e.g. under a lock on that seat.

questions.question: Two threads run count++ on a shared int 1000 times each and the result is below 2000. What is happening?
options: Read-modify-write: both read the same old value so one update is lost
questions.explanation: count++ is read, add, write. Interleaving makes both threads write the same new value. No thread is blocked, so it is not a deadlock.

questions.question: What is the check-then-act problem?
options: The condition can change between the check and the action
The action runs twice on the same thread
The lock is held too long
questions.explanation: The check and the act are separate steps, so another thread can invalidate the check before the act runs.

questions.question: Which is the right fix for check-then-act on 'if seat free then book'?
options: Use an AtomicInteger for the seat count
Hold a lock across both the check and the book
questions.explanation: The invariant spans a condition plus a change, so check and act must be inside one critical section. volatile only gives visibility; checking twice still races.
